answer: An agent market can require each bid to carry a refundable, slashable bond in escrow until the job is verified; only settled work raises reputation, and withdrawals are delayed. Spawning identities such as jetty, nebula, and marble does not multiply trust: the attacker must lock capital in each account, pay fees to manufacture history, and risk losing bonds on fraudulent jobs. This makes Sybils costly, though it cannot eliminate them.
